title: How Long Does Driveway Crack Filler Take to Dry? 1-24 Hours
h1: How Long Does Driveway Crack Filler Take to Dry?
query: how long does driveway crack filler take to dry
keywords: how long does crack filler take to dry before sealing
how long does asphalt crack filler take to dry
how long for crack filler to dry
can i seal over crack filler the same day
how long before driving on crack filler
how long does driveway caulk take to dry
description: Fast rubberized crack fillers list about 1 hour before sealing above 65°F, torch rope sets in 20 minutes, and standard fillers need up to 24 hours.
dek: Dry, firm and cured are three different waits. Here is how long each filler type takes, from the labels.
quickAnswer: Fast rubberized cold-pour fillers such as Black Jack Speed-Fill list about 1 hour before sealing in good conditions (above 65°F and under 50% humidity). Torch-melted rope such as Latex-ite Pli-Stix sets in about 20 minutes. Standard asphalt-emulsion fillers commonly need several hours to 24 hours; Latex-ite's sealer directions say wait 24 hours, or until the filler is firm. Cold-patch pothole mix needs weeks. Cool, humid weather and deep cracks make every number longer.
intro: Crack filling is the step before sealing that everyone wants to hurry. The filler you poured this morning looks black and shiny, the label says it dries in 60 minutes, the sealer pail says wait 24 hours, and last year's filler stayed soft in the middle for two days. All of those can be right, because dry means different things for different filler types, and cure time depends on crack depth, temperature and humidity.

This page gives the waits by filler type, using manufacturer label directions and technical data sheets as reference points. We have not run our own drying trials; the label on the product you buy is always the final word.

blocks.p: The practical rule for a pourable or caulk-tube filler in summer: wait until the filler is firm all the way through, not just dark on top, and give it at least the label's minimum. In warm, dry sun that can be an hour for the fastest rubberized products. In cool, cloudy or humid weather, or in a crack deeper than about half an inch, it can be a full day or longer. When in doubt, wait overnight. A filler that is soft underneath will shrink, crack or bleed through the sealer, and it is much harder to fix once the driveway is sealed.

sections.h: What Is the Difference Between Dry, Firm and Cured?

blocks.p: Crack filler labels use dry, set and cure loosely. Think of three stages.

The top has skinned over and no longer feels wet. Water-based cold-pour fillers skin over first because water leaves from the top. A skinned-over filler can still be liquid underneath, especially in a deep crack, and this is the stage at which people most often seal too soon.

The filler is set through its depth and does not dent or squeeze up when pressed. This is what most labels mean by a before-sealing time. Latex-ite's sealer data sheet puts it simply: wait 24 hours for crack fillers, and if the filler is firm you may seal over it.

The filler has reached its final flexibility and toughness. For water-based products this can take days in cool weather, but it does not usually stop you sealing over the filler once it is firm. Full cure matters most for heavy loads and turning tires.

sections.h: How Long Does Each Type of Crack Filler Take to Dry?

blocks.p: Asphalt emulsions modified with rubber or polymer, poured from a jug with a spout. They cure by evaporation, so they behave like a thick driveway sealer: fast in hot, dry sun and slow in cool, damp shade. Fast versions are formulated to be sealed over in about an hour in good conditions; standard versions more often need several hours, and the label may say wait until the next day. Fill deep cracks in layers, letting each firm up, or push in foam backer rod first. Our [driveway crack filler rankings](/best-driveway-crack-filler/) match fillers to crack widths.

The same kind of rubberized emulsion in a 10-ounce tube for a caulking gun. Because the bead is small and controlled, these often dry faster than a jug filler poured into a deep crack. Fast versions commonly list about an hour in warm, dry weather.

Rubberized asphalt rope, of which Latex-ite Pli-Stix is the best-known consumer product, is pressed into the crack and melted with a propane torch. It sets as it cools rather than by evaporation, which makes it the fastest option: Latex-ite's instructions say to let Pli-Stix set up for about 20 minutes before sealing over it. The crack still needs to be clean and dry, and the torch work needs care near grass, siding and anything flammable.

Melted in a kettle and applied hot by paving contractors. Like rope, it sets as it cools, usually quickly enough for traffic the same day. If a contractor filled your cracks this way, ask when it can be sealed over.

Thicker, sand-loaded emulsions for wider cracks and shallow low spots. Their bulk means slower drying, commonly many hours to a day or more, longer in deep spots. Follow the label and test for firmness.

Bagged cold patch for potholes is not a crack filler and cures far more slowly. Black Jack's Drive-Maxx sealer data sheets say its permanent pothole patch should cure for six weeks before sealing. Many cold-patch products give similar multi-week waits, so check yours. For holes and failing areas, see [how to fix a crumbling asphalt driveway](/how-to-fix-crumbling-asphalt-driveway/).

sections.h: What Do the Crack Filler Labels Actually Say?

blocks.p: Specific label directions show how much these products differ. These come from the makers' published technical data sheets.

ul: Black Jack Speed-Fill Elastic Crack Filler (1-gallon jug): a fast-drying rubberized compound for cracks and joints up to 3/4 inch wide. Allow 1 hour in good drying conditions, defined as above 65°F and under 50% relative humidity, before coating with a premium driveway sealer. Humidity and cool air or surface temperatures may lengthen the cure. Apply at 65°F and rising, not if rain is expected within 24 hours. Pour slightly above the crack to allow for settling; deeper cracks need a second application. A 3.6-quart fill is listed for about 75 linear feet of 1/4-inch cracks.

Black Jack Speed-Fill Blacktop Filler (10-ounce tube): marketed as drying in 60 minutes, for cracks up to 1 inch. Apply on a clear sunny day with the surface at 65°F and rising, make sure it has cured before sealing, and do not apply if rain is expected within 12 hours. One tube gives about 32 linear feet of 1/4-inch bead.
Latex-ite Pli-Stix: let the melted rope set up for about 20 minutes before sealing over it.
Latex-ite sealer directions: the Airport Grade data sheet says to let all repaired surfaces cure 24 hours before sealing, and for crack fillers to wait 24 hours, or seal over once the filler is firm.

Black Jack sealer directions: the Drive-Maxx sheets say to repair cracks with Speed-Fill, use Speed-Patch for cracks and holes over 1 inch, and let every repair cure to its own product instructions, with six weeks for the permanent pothole patch.

blocks.p: The pattern is clear: the fastest products are fast only in warm, dry conditions, and even the makers that sell them fall back on until firm or 24 hours in their general guidance.

sections.h: What Makes Crack Filler Take Longer to Dry?

ul: Temperature: water-based fillers cure by evaporation, which slows sharply in the cold. Many labels set a 50°F minimum, and fast products like Speed-Fill ask for 65°F and rising to hit their quoted times. A cool night after a warm day can stall a cure.
Humidity: high humidity slows evaporation even on a warm day. Speed-Fill's one-hour figure assumes under 50% relative humidity; on a muggy morning, expect several times longer.

Depth and width: a deep crack filled in one pour can skin over in an hour and stay soft underneath for a day or more. Fill in layers, or set backer rod to within about half an inch of the surface first.
Shade and sun angle: shaded areas and the low sun of spring and fall slow curing noticeably.
Moisture in the crack: filling a crack still wet from rinsing or rain dilutes the filler and traps water. Speed-Fill's sheet says to rinse the crack and let it dry before filling.
Rain: Speed-Fill wants 24 hours without rain, the tube version 12. Rain on fresh cold-pour filler can wash it out of the crack or leave a gray, weak skin.

blocks.p: For the temperature rules that apply to the sealer coat as well, see [what temperature to seal a driveway](/what-temperature-to-seal-driveway/).

sections.h: How Long Should Crack Filler Dry Before Sealing?

blocks.p: Use the longest of three numbers: the crack filler label's before-sealing time, the sealer label's rule for repaired areas (24 hours or until firm for Latex-ite; the repair product's own cure time for Black Jack), and the time it takes the filler to pass a firmness check.

In practice: on a warm, dry, sunny day with a fast filler in shallow cracks, you can often fill in the morning and seal in the afternoon. With a standard filler, deep cracks or cool or humid weather, fill one day and seal the next. The safest weekend plan is clean and fill on Saturday, seal on Sunday, or fill the weekend before. The sealer then needs its own rain-free window; see [rain after sealing a driveway](/rain-after-sealing-driveway/).

Sealing too soon causes three problems. The sealer can trap moisture in the filler and leave it soft and gummy. The filler can shrink as it finishes curing and pull a dip or crack in the sealer above it. And the sealer can absorb dark oils from uncured filler and show lines. All three are avoided by waiting.

sections.h: How Long Before You Can Drive on Crack Filler?

blocks.p: If you are not sealing straight away, keep cars off fresh cold-pour filler for at least 24 hours in good weather, longer in cool or humid weather, and avoid turning the wheels on it for a few days. Turning tires scuff soft filler out of the crack. Rope and hot-pour fillers can usually take traffic sooner because they set as they cool, but they can soften on a hot afternoon.

If you are sealing the driveway, the sealer's own wait takes over, commonly 24 to 48 hours for vehicles. Our guide to [how long driveway sealer takes to dry](/how-long-for-driveway-sealer-to-dry/) covers that wait and heavier vehicles.

sections.h: How Can You Tell When Crack Filler Is Ready?

ul: The press test: press a fingertip or the end of a wooden stick into the middle of the filled crack. If it dents and does not spring back, or liquid shows at the edges, it is not ready. If it is firm and only slightly flexible, like a rubber eraser, it is ready to seal over.
Color and sheen: most cold-pour fillers go from brown or glossy to a uniform dull black as they dry. A brown or wet-looking center means the middle is still curing.
The deepest spot: test the widest, deepest section, not the edges. It is the last part to cure.
Settling: if the filler has sunk well below the surface, top it up and wait again. Speed-Fill's directions expect this: fill slightly proud and add a second pour to deep cracks.

mistakes: A cold-pour filler that looks black on top can still be liquid below. Seal over it and the filler stays gummy, shrinks into a dip or bleeds lines through the new coat. Press-test the deepest spot before any sealer goes down.
Filling a deep crack in one pour
A single deep pour skins over and stays soft underneath for a day or more, then settles. Push in backer rod to about half an inch below the surface, or fill in layers and let each firm up.
Heating cold-pour filler with a torch
Black Jack's Speed-Fill labels say do not heat. Torches are only for rope fillers designed to be melted. Speed up a cold-pour filler by choosing a warm, dry, sunny day, not by applying flame.
The sealer label has its own rule for repaired areas, such as Latex-ite's 24 hours or until firm. Use the longest of the filler's time, the sealer's rule and a firmness check.
bottomLine: Driveway crack filler can be ready in 20 minutes or need a full day, depending on type and weather. Torch-melted rope such as Pli-Stix sets in about 20 minutes; fast rubberized cold-pour fillers such as Speed-Fill list about an hour above 65°F and under 50% humidity; standard emulsion fillers often need up to 24 hours, which is also Latex-ite's general rule for repairs before sealing. Test the deepest spot for firmness, use the longest of the label times, and when in doubt fill one day and seal the next.

faqs.q: How long does driveway crack filler take to dry before sealing?
faqs.a: It depends on the filler. Fast rubberized cold-pour fillers like Black Jack Speed-Fill list about 1 hour in good conditions (above 65°F, under 50% humidity). Torch-melted rope like Latex-ite Pli-Stix sets in about 20 minutes. Standard emulsion fillers commonly need several hours to 24 hours. When in doubt, wait until the deepest part is firm; Latex-ite's sealer directions say 24 hours, or until firm.

faqs.q: How long does driveway caulk take to dry?
faqs.a: Caulk-tube driveway fillers are usually rubberized asphalt emulsions that dry by evaporation. Fast versions such as Black Jack Speed-Fill Blacktop Filler are marketed to dry in about 60 minutes on a clear day at 65°F and rising; others need longer. Household caulk is a different product; see our guide to how long caulk takes to dry.

faqs.q: Can I seal over crack filler the same day?
faqs.a: Yes, with a fast-drying filler in shallow cracks on a warm, dry, sunny day, once the filler is firm through its depth. With standard fillers, deep cracks, or cool or humid weather, fill one day and seal the next.

faqs.q: What happens if I seal over crack filler that isn't dry?
faqs.a: The filler can stay soft and gummy, shrink and pull a dip or crack in the sealer above it, or bleed dark lines through it. Fixing it means scraping out the filler and sealer in that spot and redoing both, so it pays to wait.

faqs.q: Does crack filler dry faster with heat?
faqs.a: Warm, dry, sunny weather speeds up cold-pour fillers. Do not heat a cold-pour filler with a torch, though: Black Jack's Speed-Fill labels say do not heat. Torches are only for rope fillers designed to be melted, such as Pli-Stix.

faqs.q: How long before I can drive on crack filler?
faqs.a: Keep vehicles off fresh cold-pour filler for at least 24 hours in good weather and avoid turning on it for a few days. If you seal the driveway, follow the sealer's vehicle wait, commonly 24 to 48 hours.

faqs.q: How long does cold patch take to cure before sealing?
faqs.a: Much longer than crack filler. Black Jack's sealer data sheets say its permanent pothole patch needs six weeks to cure before sealing, and many cold-patch products give similar multi-week waits. Check the bag of the product you used.
